subject: Compatibility scouting recap & qualification — Medicaid migration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Compatibility scouting recap & qualification — Medicaid migration

Claire, thanks again for your time today — appreciate the clear description of the constraints. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align the technical POC scope.

Key pain points you called out
- Token costs are spiking under current OpenAI/Anthropic usage for high-volume clinical note generation (~10M tokens/mo).
- Hard latency requirement for some patient-facing workflows (<150ms median, <300ms p95).
- Data governance: logs must remain in-customer (VPC-hosted control plane) and audit trails for each request.
- Model compatibility: some existing prompt templates assume OpenAI/ChatCompletion API shapes and function-calling semantics.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary: OpenAI (gpt-4o-ish) for generation, Anthropic for assistant/safety flows.
- Orchestration: internal proxy that normalizes responses and applies prompt transforms.
- Authentication: SSO + API keys; KMS for encryption of stored artifacts.

Success criteria for an initial POC
- API parity for your 3 canonical prompt templates (format + function-call style).
- Latency: median < 150ms for 1024-token outputs on our estimated test profile.
- Cost: forecasted per-token cost improvement >= 25% vs current spend at target scale.
- Security: deployment in VPC with customer-controlled KMS and audit logs.

Model shortlist we discussed (preliminary)
- Llama 3 / 70B quantized variant (fast prefix KV and good instruction-following after RLHF).
- Mistral-Instruct family (lighter memory footprint for similar quality).
- One Anthropic-compatible instruction-tuned family to minimize prompt rework.

Open questions for you to confirm
1) Can your infra team provide a small sample of the most-used prompts and expected sequence-length distributions (token histogram)?
2) Any non-negotiable third-party vetting (e.g., internal security review with SOC2 type II evidence)?
3) Procurement timing / POC purchase order process and budget guardrails?

Proposed next steps
- We’ll share a short compatibility matrix (attached) showing API parity and required adapter work per model.
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra and security leads (proposed slots Tue/Wed next week).
- Redwood to produce a one-week test harness (sample dataset, synthetic load, latency/cost dashboard) for the POC.

Attachments: compatibility-matrix.xlsx (high level), redwood-poc-outline.pdf (POC scope).

If this looks right, confirm the technical owner(s) to include and preferred time windows for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Internal notes / qualification (quick):
- Medicaid looks like a strong mid-market enterprise ARR profile; timeline likely 60–90 days for POC + security review.
- Procurement cadence: we’ll need an SOW + short PO; Carlos will push for a capped spend POC. Price sensitivity: aim to present a 3-tier POC option (baseline / optimized-batch / premium low-latency).
- Risk flags: HIPAA / PHI handling — ensure our private deployment option (Redwood Private) and KMS/HSM details are front-and-center.
- Recommended PoC: 2-week functional + 2-week load verification with a target dataset capped at 100k prompt units. Use one quantized Llama variant and one Mistral-Instruct for comparison.

Action items for Ben:
1) Draft POC SOW (one-pager) + three-tier pricing options.
2) Prepare short list of SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes for Carlos & security.
3) Share proposed engineer/architect attendees for the deep-dive (Tom + their platform engineer).
